jurisdictions.name: United States - Federal
jurisdictions.general_notes: Psilocybin, LSD, MDMA, DMT, 5-MeO-DMT, mescaline, peyote and ibogaine are Schedule I controlled substances (21 CFR 1308.11). The federal Right to Try pathway lets patients with a life-threatening disease who have exhausted approved options and cannot join a trial seek investigational drugs; FDA also runs an Expanded Access program. Applicable clinical trials initiated after September 27, 2007 must be registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (42 CFR 11.22).

procedures.description: MDMA (midomafetamine) given with manualized therapy for PTSD. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (Mitchell et al., Nature Medicine 2021) found a significant reduction in CAPS-5 score versus placebo (d = 0.91). procedures.name: Ibogaine Treatment for Opioid/Substance Use Disorder
procedures.description: Ibogaine, an indole alkaloid from the root of the Central African shrub Tabernanthe iboga, used mainly to interrupt opioid withdrawal and addiction; observational studies report rapid reduction of opioid withdrawal, but no randomized controlled trials exist. The acute psychoactive phase can last about 24-38 hours. QT-interval prolongation (hERG blockade) creates a narrow therapeutic window and serious arrhythmia risk. Ibogaine is Schedule I in the US and has no authorised medicinal product in the EU.

procedures.name: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) / Assisted Death
procedures.description: Medical assistance in dying covers clinician-administered euthanasia and self-administered assisted suicide. Statutory frameworks include Canada (Criminal Code MAID provisions; extra safeguards when death is not reasonably foreseeable; people whose only condition is mental illness are not eligible until March 17, 2027), the Netherlands (Termination of Life on Request and Assisted Suicide (Review Procedures) Act), Belgium (Law of 28 May 2002 on euthanasia) and Spain (Organic Law 3/2021). In Germany the Federal Constitutional Court voided the ban on professionalised suicide assistance in 2020. Eligibility and safeguards differ by jurisdiction.

procedures.description: Methylene blue (methylthioninium chloride) is an authorised medicine for acute drug- or chemical-induced methaemoglobinaemia (e.g. EU Proveblue). access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: Psilocybin services are provided at licensed psilocybin service centers under ORS 475A (Ballot Measure 109). Adults 21+ can access services without a prescription or medical referral. A preparation session with a licensed facilitator is required before an administration session, which must take place at a service center; facilitators follow up within 72 hours and offer integration sessions.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Must be 21 or older. Oregon residency is not required, and no prescription, medical referral or diagnosis is required. Facilitators may decline services, and certain answers on the Client Information Form can make a client ineligible.
access_records.provider_requirements: Facilitators must hold an OHA facilitator license (age 21+, high school diploma or equivalent, OHA-approved training, and a passed examination); OHA may not require a degree. Administration sessions must be held at a licensed psilocybin service center. Products are tested by licensed laboratories that must first be ORELAP-accredited.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: No residency requirement: clients do not need to live in Oregon. Psilocybin can only be purchased and consumed at a licensed service center during an administration session; products may not be taken off-site, and clients stay a minimum time based on dose.
access_records.risk_notes: Products are tested for species identity and psilocybin potency; testing for microbials, heavy metals or pesticides is at OPS's discretion rather than routine. Facilitators may decline services, and some answers on the Client Information Form can make a client ineligible.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: State-licensed psilocybin services open to adults 21+ without a prescription, referral or Oregon residency. Psilocybin remains Schedule I under federal law.
access_records.oversight_notes: The Oregon Health Authority's Oregon Psilocybin Services Section licenses and regulates manufacturers, service centers, facilitators and laboratories under ORS 475A. Laboratories test products for Psilocybe cubensis identity and psilocybin potency.
access_records.cost_notes: Prices are set by each service center and facilitator; Oregon Psilocybin Services does not set or regulate the costs of psilocybin products or services.
access_records.legal_basis: ORS chapter 475A (Oregon Psilocybin Services Act, Ballot Measure 109, 2020): OHA licenses manufacturers, service centers, facilitators and laboratories; clients 21+; administration sessions only at licensed service centers. Psilocybin remains federally Schedule I.

access_records.procedure_name: DMT (N,N-Dimethyltryptamine) Assisted Therapy for Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: Colorado law (C.R.S. 18-18-434, SB23-290) provides that a person who, for personal use and without remuneration, possesses, consumes, shares, cultivates or manufactures natural DMT does not violate state law; synthetic DMT is excluded. DMT is not part of the licensed healing-centre programme unless the Natural Medicine Advisory Board recommends it and state regulators approve it for inclusion on or after 1 June 2026. DMT remains Schedule I under federal law.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults 21+; personal use without remuneration. Under-21 possession or consumption is a drug petty offense.

access_records.residency_travel_notes: The personal-use provision applies to any person and is not limited to Colorado residents; federal law still applies.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Colorado decriminalises personal use of natural DMT for adults 21+; there is no licensed DMT therapy unless regulators add DMT to the programme. Federal Schedule I still applies.
access_records.oversight_notes: Personal-use DMT falls outside the state's licensed cultivation, testing and dispensing system, which applies only to regulated natural medicine.
access_records.legal_basis: C.R.S. 18-18-434 as enacted by SB23-290 (2023 Sess. Laws ch. 249): personal-use possession, consumption, sharing, cultivation and manufacture of natural (non-synthetic) DMT without remuneration does not violate state law; under-21 possession is a drug petty offense. access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: Since 1 July 2023, specialist psychiatrists authorised by the TGA under the Authorised Prescriber scheme can prescribe psilocybine for treatment-resistant depression as part of psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy. Psilocybine products remain unapproved medicines that are not included in the ARTG.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Patients with treatment-resistant depression treated by an Authorised Prescriber psychiatrist under a clinical treatment protocol approved by a registered human research ethics committee, with informed consent.
access_records.provider_requirements: The prescriber must be registered as a specialist psychiatrist with the Medical Board of Australia, obtain HREC approval of a clinical treatment protocol, and be authorised by the TGA for each product through the SAS and Authorised Prescriber Online System. RANZCP has published a training framework for psychiatrists seeking authorisation.
access_records.risk_notes: Psilocybine products have not been evaluated by the TGA for quality, safety and efficacy.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Prescriber-level authorised access to unapproved psilocybine for treatment-resistant depression through TGA-authorised psychiatrists; no psilocybine product is registered on the ARTG.
access_records.oversight_notes: The TGA authorises each prescriber and product under the Authorised Prescriber scheme, which requires prior ethics committee (HREC) approval of the treatment protocol.
access_records.legal_basis: Poisons Standard: from 1 July 2023 psilocybine is a Schedule 8 controlled drug only when prescribed for treatment-resistant depression by a psychiatrist authorised under the TGA Authorised Prescriber scheme; all other uses remain Schedule 9 (prohibited). Psilocybine products are unapproved medicines not included in the ARTG.

access_records.procedure_name: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) / Assisted Death
access_records.access_pathway_details: MAID is lawful in Canada under the Criminal Code. Where natural death is not reasonably foreseeable, there must be at least 90 clear days between the first assessment and provision (shorter only if capacity loss is imminent). People whose sole underlying condition is a mental illness are not eligible until March 17, 2027. Physicians and, where provincially allowed, nurse practitioners assess and provide MAID.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Must be eligible for government-funded health services in Canada (or would be, but for a minimum residency or waiting period). At least 18 and mentally competent. Grievous and irremediable medical condition. Voluntary request and informed consent. Written request signed and dated by one independent witness. Minimum 90-day assessment where natural death is not reasonably foreseeable.
access_records.provider_requirements: Physicians, and nurse practitioners in provinces where this is allowed, may conduct assessments and provide MAID.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: Eligibility is tied to government-funded health coverage in Canada; a provincial minimum residency or waiting period does not by itself bar eligibility. People who are not, and would not be, eligible for such coverage cannot access MAID.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Canada does not require a terminal diagnosis (a separate safeguard track applies where death is not reasonably foreseeable), but access is limited to people eligible for government-funded health services in Canada.
access_records.oversight_notes: Statutory safeguards include a written request witnessed by an independent witness and, where natural death is not reasonably foreseeable, a minimum 90-clear-day assessment period.
access_records.legal_basis: Criminal Code (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46), s. 241.2 (medical assistance in dying)
access_records.regulatory_authority: Health Canada (federal) under the Criminal Code; delivered by physicians and nurse practitioners

access_records.procedure_name: LSD-Assisted Psychotherapy for Anxiety Disorders
access_records.access_pathway_details: Under Art. 8(5) of the Narcotics Act (BetmG), the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) grants treating physicians case-by-case exceptional permits for limited medical use of LSD, MDMA or psilocybin in individual patients. Each permit covers one patient and one substance, is valid for one year and may be renewed; there is no entitlement to a permit.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Serious illness where conventional treatments have been exhausted and relief can be expected. Anxiety disorders are among the most common primary indications. The physician's application includes the patient's written consent.
access_records.provider_requirements: Only the treating physician can apply to the BAG. Permit holders are usually specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy; parts of the treatment can be delegated to other professionals.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Switzerland permits limited medical use of LSD through BAG per-patient exceptional permits requested by the treating physician; not a marketing authorisation.
access_records.oversight_notes: BAG per-patient exceptional permit system in place since 2014; about 1,800 permits (initial and renewals) were issued from 2014 to the end of 2024. It is an exception under narcotics law, not a marketing authorisation.
access_records.cost_notes: Billing within the Swiss tariff system is not regulated; patients mostly pay the costs themselves.
access_records.legal_basis: Betäubungsmittelgesetz (BetmG, SR 812.121) Art. 8 Abs. 5 — BAG exceptional permits for limited medical use of prohibited narcotics

access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: Practitioners can request psilocybin for an individual patient through Health Canada's Special Access Program when the patient has a serious or life-threatening condition and conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable. Individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions are another route, generally only where clinical trials or the SAP are not possible or suitable. No psilocybin product is approved in Canada.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Serious or life-threatening condition for which conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable; the request is made by the treating practitioner on a patient-specific form.
access_records.provider_requirements: The requesting practitioner must be licensed to prescribe in their province or territory. The drug must come from a licensed dealer, and imported product needs a Health Canada import permit.
access_records.risk_notes: An SAP authorization is not a Health Canada finding that the drug is safe or effective.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Case-by-case federal access through the Special Access Program or a subsection 56(1) exemption for patients with serious conditions; not an open or commercial market.
access_records.oversight_notes: Health Canada reviews each SAP request case by case. A subsection 56(1) class exemption lets practitioners, pharmacists, hospitals and licensed dealers handle SAP-authorized psilocybin; Health Canada states it will be revoked when new Controlled Substances Regulations take effect on 1 October 2026.
access_records.legal_basis: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act: production, sale and possession of psilocybin are illegal unless authorized by Health Canada. Psilocybin is a restricted drug obtainable for individual patients through the Special Access Program (serious or life-threatening conditions where conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable) or individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions. No approved psilocybin product.

access_records.procedure_name: Ketamine Infusion Therapy for Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: IV ketamine for depression is off-label: ketamine is FDA-approved only as a general anaesthetic (Schedule III). Esketamine nasal spray (Spravato) is FDA-approved for treatment-resistant depression and is available only through the SPRAVATO REMS in certified healthcare settings.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Spravato (FDA label): adults with treatment-resistant depression, or depressive symptoms in MDD with acute suicidal ideation or behaviour (with an oral antidepressant). Contraindicated in aneurysmal vascular disease, arteriovenous malformation or intracerebral haemorrhage. IV ketamine use for depression is off-label.
access_records.provider_requirements: Spravato: dispensed and administered only in REMS-certified healthcare settings, with patient monitoring for at least 2 hours after each dose. IV ketamine: ordinary prescribing and DEA Schedule III registration rules; no REMS.
access_records.risk_notes: Spravato labelling warns of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, and abuse and misuse; patients must be monitored for at least 2 hours after each dose. FDA has warned about compounded ketamine products used for psychiatric disorders.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Off-label IV ketamine under federal Schedule III rules; FDA-approved Spravato via REMS-certified settings.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal: ketamine is Schedule III (DEA); Spravato is subject to an FDA REMS. Off-label IV ketamine has no REMS.
access_records.legal_basis: Ketamine: FDA-approved general anaesthetic (Ketalar, NDA 016812), Schedule III under 21 CFR 1308.13(c)(7); not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder, so depression use is off-label. Esketamine (Spravato, NDA 211243) FDA-approved for TRD and MDD with acute suicidal ideation under the SPRAVATO REMS.

access_records.procedure_name: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide / Tirzepatide) Beyond Diabetes
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA-approved beyond diabetes: Wegovy (semaglutide injection and tablets) for weight reduction, cardiovascular risk reduction and MASH; Zepbound (tirzepatide) for weight reduction and obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity. FDA declared the semaglutide shortage resolved on 21 Feb 2025; enforcement discretion for 503A compounders has ended and for 503B outsourcing facilities ran until 22 May 2025 (semaglutide) and 19 Mar 2025 (tirzepatide). On 30 Apr 2026 FDA proposed excluding semaglutide and tirzepatide from the 503B bulks list.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Labelled for adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbid condition (Wegovy also adolescents 12+ with obesity); Zepbound also for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Contraindicated with personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
access_records.risk_notes: Boxed warning: thyroid C-cell tumours in rodents. Labelled warnings include acute pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, hypoglycaemia with insulin or secretagogues, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, severe gastrointestinal reactions, diabetic retinopathy complications, heart-rate increase and pulmonary aspiration under anaesthesia. Most common adverse reactions are gastrointestinal (nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: GLP-1 receptor agonists are FDA-approved for weight reduction and other non-diabetes indications; shortage-era compounding of copies is no longer covered by enforcement discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-approved products with labelled boxed warning. Shortage-based compounding enforcement discretion ended in 2025 after FDA found the semaglutide and tirzepatide shortages resolved; a 30 Apr 2026 proposal would exclude both from the 503B bulks list (final decision pending).
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approvals of Wegovy (semaglutide: weight reduction, CV risk reduction, MASH) and Zepbound (tirzepatide: weight reduction, OSA in obesity)

access_records.procedure_name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) for Longevity/Healthspan
access_records.access_pathway_details: Sirolimus (Rapamune and generic tablets) is FDA-approved, prescription-only, for prophylaxis of organ rejection in renal transplant patients aged 13 and over and for lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM). Use for ageing/longevity is off-label and needs a prescription from a licensed prescriber.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: No regulatory eligibility criteria for off-label use; the prescriber judges whether it is medically appropriate for the patient.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (prescription-only drug). The label recommends therapeutic drug monitoring for all patients.
access_records.risk_notes: US label boxed warning: immunosuppression may increase susceptibility to infection and possible development of lymphoma and other malignancies. Label warnings include impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia, proteinuria, interstitial lung disease, embryo-fetal toxicity and male infertility; avoid strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors or inducers and live vaccines. Common adverse reactions in LAM patients include stomatitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and hypercholesterolemia. Labelled safety data come from transplant and LAM patients, not longevity dosing.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: sirolimus is an FDA-approved generic prescription drug; prescribing it for longevity is lawful off-label use at the prescriber's discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA approves the drug and its labelling; FDA states that once a drug is approved, providers generally may prescribe it for an unapproved use when they judge it medically appropriate.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved prescription drug (Rapamune NDA 021083; generic sirolimus ANDAs) indicated for renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and LAM; longevity use is off-label, which FDA says providers generally may prescribe when medically appropriate

access_records.procedure_name: Gestational Surrogacy
access_records.access_pathway_details: Surrogacy is lawful in Canada only on an unpaid (altruistic) basis. Paying, offering to pay or advertising payment to a surrogate is prohibited, as is paying or accepting payment to arrange a surrogate. Surrogates may be reimbursed for documented surrogacy-related expenditures listed in federal regulations. The validity of surrogacy agreements and parentage are matters of provincial law.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: It is an offence to counsel or induce a woman under 21 to become a surrogate, or to perform a medical procedure to help her become one.
access_records.provider_requirements: Reimbursement requires a receipt for each expenditure; lost work income can be reimbursed only with a signed declaration, supporting evidence and medical certification.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Canada permits altruistic surrogacy with expense reimbursement only; commercial surrogacy and paid brokering are federal offences.
access_records.oversight_notes: Health Canada administers and enforces the Assisted Human Reproduction Act. Reimbursable expenditure categories (travel, dependant care, groceries, maternity clothes, insurance, legal and counselling services, among others) were defined by regulations that took effect in 2020. Provincial law governs agreements and parentage.

access_records.procedure_name: CRISPR-Based Gene Therapy (Somatic) for Genetic Disorders
access_records.access_pathway_details: Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel), the first FDA-approved CRISPR/Cas9 therapy, is approved for patients aged 2 years and older with sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises or transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia. Investigational CRISPR therapies may be sought through FDA Expanded Access or the federal Right to Try Act.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Casgevy: Patients aged 2 years and older with sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, or transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia. Right to Try: life-threatening disease, approved options exhausted, unable to join a trial, written informed consent; the drug must have completed Phase 1 and not be FDA-approved for any use.
access_records.risk_notes: Requires myeloablative conditioning (high-dose chemotherapy) before infusion of the patient's edited stem cells; most common side effects include low platelet and white blood cell counts, mouth sores and nausea. Treated patients are followed in a long-term safety study.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: Casgevy is FDA-approved for SCD and TDT (age 2+); other CRISPR therapies are investigational and reachable via Expanded Access or Right to Try only if the sponsor agrees.
access_records.oversight_notes: Casgevy is FDA-approved with long-term follow-up of treated patients. Under Right to Try, sponsors are not required to provide investigational drugs.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approval of Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel): 8 Dec 2023 (SCD), 16 Jan 2024 (TDT); label extended to patients aged 2+ in 2026. Investigational CRISPR therapies: FDA Expanded Access or the federal Right to Try Act (2018).

access_records.estimated_cost_range_usd: $350–2,815 per injection (median $800; top-ranked US orthopedic hospitals, 2023 survey)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Most PRP preparation systems are FDA 510(k)-cleared for producing PRP to be mixed with bone graft material in orthopedic practice; office injection of PRP outside that setting is off-label use of the device. As a blood product, PRP itself is exempt from the traditional FDA regulatory pathway.
access_records.risk_notes: Insurer medical policy (FEP Blue, 2026) considers PRP investigational for all orthopedic indications.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: PRP offered as off-label use of cleared devices, usually cash-pay, with wide price variation between institutions.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA regulates PRP preparation devices through 510(k) clearance; PRP as a blood product is exempt from the traditional FDA regulatory pathway.
access_records.cost_notes: Self-pay is typical: the Federal Employee Program policy treats PRP as investigational for all orthopedic indications. A 2023 survey of top US orthopedic hospitals found prices of $350–2,815 per injection, highest in the Northeast.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA 510(k) device clearance (bone-graft handling indication); off-label use of legally marketed devices preserved by 21 U.S.C. § 396
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (510(k) clearance of PRP preparation devices); PRP itself exempt from traditional FDA pathway

access_records.procedure_name: Elective Oocyte Cryopreservation (Social Egg Freezing)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Elective (non-medical) egg freezing is offered as a self-pay or insurance-covered procedure at US fertility clinics. It is lawful medical practice, not a product approval.
access_records.risk_notes: Ovarian stimulation can rarely cause ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). Freezing eggs does not guarantee a future pregnancy.
access_records.oversight_notes: Clinics performing ART must report cycle data to CDC under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992. FDA rules for human cells and tissues (21 CFR 1271) apply, with autologous use exempt from donor-eligibility screening.
access_records.cost_notes: Some but not all insurance plans cover elective egg freezing; otherwise it is self-pay.
access_records.legal_basis: Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992 (CDC reporting); 21 CFR Part 1271 (HCT/Ps). No federal statute restricts elective oocyte cryopreservation.
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (HCT/P rules, 21 CFR 1271); CDC (ART reporting); state medical boards

access_records.procedure_name: Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy uses ketamine off-label: ketamine is FDA-approved only as a general anaesthetic (Schedule III) and is not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder. access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: KAP relies on off-label ketamine under federal Schedule III rules.

access_records.legal_basis: Ketamine: FDA-approved general anaesthetic (Ketalar, NDA 016812), Schedule III under 21 CFR 1308.13(c)(7); not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder, so depression use is off-label. Esketamine (Spravato, NDA 211243) FDA-approved for TRD and MDD with acute suicidal ideation under the SPRAVATO REMS.

access_records.procedure_name: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) for HIV Lipodystrophy / Off-Label Visceral Fat
access_records.access_pathway_details: Egrifta (tesamorelin; current Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR formulations) is FDA-approved to reduce excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. Because it is a licensed biological product, pharmacy-compounding exemptions do not apply.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: FDA label: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat; contraindicated with disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, active malignancy, or pregnancy.
access_records.provider_requirements: Prescription required.
access_records.risk_notes: Label warnings include glucose intolerance or diabetes, raised IGF-1, fluid retention and hypersensitivity; common reactions include arthralgia, injection-site erythema and peripheral oedema.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: FDA-approved tesamorelin by prescription for HIV lipodystrophy; no lawful compounded version.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-licensed biological product (deemed a BLA since March 2020); the FD&C Act s.503A/503B compounding exemptions do not cover biological products.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approval of Egrifta (tesamorelin), application 022505, 10 Nov 2010; deemed a biologics licence (BLA) under the BPCI Act on 23 March 2020

access_records.procedure_name: Dendritic Cell Cancer Vaccines (Personalized)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Personalized dendritic cell vaccines are advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs). In the EU, ATMPs may be supplied legally only if centrally authorised via EMA, given in a clinical trial authorised by a national authority, or used in a hospital under a national hospital exemption; Germany has a national hospital-exemption framework. Provenge's EU marketing authorisation was withdrawn in 2015. In Germany, hospital-exemption supply requires PEI authorisation under § 4b AMG; PEI granted such an authorisation for the DC vaccine DCVax-L (glioma) in 2014.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Clinical-trial criteria, or an individual patient's medical prescription for a custom-made product under the hospital exemption.
access_records.provider_requirements: Hospital-exemption products are prepared on a non-routine basis to specific quality standards and used in a hospital under the exclusive professional responsibility of a medical practitioner.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: Hospital-exemption products must be used in a hospital within the same Member State.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Germany: DC vaccines only via authorised clinical trials or the national hospital exemption.
access_records.oversight_notes: EMA and the Heads of Medicines Agencies warned in March 2025 that some unregulated products in the EU are sold as dendritic cell therapies for cancer.
access_records.legal_basis: § 4b Arzneimittelgesetz (hospital exemption, PEI authorisation required); Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007

access_records.procedure_name: Elamipretide / Mitochondrial-Targeted Peptides (SS-31 Class)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Elamipretide (Forzinity) received FDA accelerated approval on 19 Sep 2025 to improve muscle strength in Barth syndrome patients weighing at least 30 kg; it is dispensed through AnovoRx, the exclusive US specialty pharmacy. access_records.provider_requirements: Prescription; supplied through the exclusive US specialty pharmacy (AnovoRx).
access_records.risk_notes: Most common adverse reactions are injection site reactions; serious reactions have been reported. Contraindicated with serious hypersensitivity to any ingredient; contains benzyl alcohol (not for use in neonates).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: FDA-approved for Barth syndrome (30 kg and over); other uses, including anti-aging, are investigational.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA accelerated approval; a post-approval randomized, placebo-controlled confirmatory trial is required.
access_records.legal_basis: NDA 215244 (Forzinity, elamipretide): FDA accelerated approval 19 Sep 2025 for Barth syndrome in patients weighing at least 30 kg; post-approval confirmatory trial required

access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: The BAG can grant case-by-case exceptional authorisations for limited medical use of prohibited narcotics such as psilocybin. In 2024 it issued 322 psilocybin authorisations; depressive disorders were the most common indication (233 psilocybin authorisations).
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Case by case: only the treating physician can apply to the BAG, with the patient's written consent.
access_records.provider_requirements: Treating physician holding a BAG exceptional authorisation; Swissmedic can issue the import permit on the basis of that authorisation. Around 100 physicians held authorisations at the end of 2024.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Physician-initiated, case-by-case authorised access under the BAG limited-medical-use scheme; not an open or commercial market.
access_records.oversight_notes: Each treatment requires a BAG exceptional authorisation, usually valid for 12 months and covering several sessions with one substance.
access_records.cost_notes: Mandatory health insurance covers only the psychotherapy, not the supervision of the long substance sessions.
access_records.legal_basis: Narcotics Act (BetmG): psilocybin is a prohibited narcotic, but the BAG can grant case-by-case exceptional authorisations for limited medical use, applied for by the treating physician with the patient's written consent; Swissmedic issues any import permit on that basis.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Federal Office of Public Health (BAG/FOPH) exceptional authorisations; Swissmedic import permits

access_records.procedure_name: MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for PTSD
access_records.access_pathway_details: Under Art. 8(5) of the Narcotics Act (BetmG), the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG) grants treating physicians case-by-case exceptional permits for limited medical use of LSD, MDMA or psilocybin in individual patients. Each permit covers one patient and one substance, is valid for one year and may be renewed; there is no entitlement to a permit.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Serious illness where conventional treatments have been exhausted and relief can be expected. Post-traumatic stress disorder is among the most common primary indications. The physician's application includes the patient's written consent.
access_records.provider_requirements: Only the treating physician can apply to the BAG. Permit holders are usually specialists in psychiatry and psychotherapy; parts of the treatment can be delegated to other professionals.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Switzerland permits limited medical use of MDMA through BAG per-patient exceptional permits requested by the treating physician; not a marketing authorisation.
access_records.oversight_notes: BAG per-patient exceptional permit system in place since 2014; about 1,800 permits (initial and renewals) were issued from 2014 to the end of 2024. It is an exception under narcotics law, not a marketing authorisation.
access_records.cost_notes: Billing within the Swiss tariff system is not regulated; patients mostly pay the costs themselves.
access_records.legal_basis: Betäubungsmittelgesetz (BetmG, SR 812.121) Art. 8 Abs. 5 — BAG exceptional permits for limited medical use of prohibited narcotics

access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: Psilocybin is a Schedule I substance under the 1971 UN Convention, to which the UAE is a party; UAE narcotics law (Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2021) controls listed substances and prohibits consumption except under a prescription.
access_records.risk_notes: Personal use or possession of scheduled narcotics or psychotropics carries at least three months' imprisonment or a fine of AED 20,000–100,000 for a first offence (Art. 41).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: No lawful therapeutic access pathway identified; criminal penalties apply.
access_records.legal_basis: Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2021 on Combating Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances (ten annexed schedules); Psilocybin is in Schedule I of the 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances, to which the UAE acceded in 1988.

access_records.procedure_name: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for End-of-Life Anxiety
access_records.access_pathway_details: Psilocybin for end-of-life distress can be requested case by case: Practitioners can request psilocybin for an individual patient through Health Canada's Special Access Program when the patient has a serious or life-threatening condition and conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable. Individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions are another route, generally only where clinical trials or the SAP are not possible or suitable. No psilocybin product is approved in Canada.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Serious or life-threatening condition for which conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable; the request is made by the treating practitioner on a patient-specific form.
access_records.provider_requirements: The requesting practitioner must be licensed to prescribe in their province or territory. The drug must come from a licensed dealer, and imported product needs a Health Canada import permit.
access_records.risk_notes: An SAP authorization is not a Health Canada finding that the drug is safe or effective.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Case-by-case federal access through the Special Access Program or a subsection 56(1) exemption for patients with serious conditions; not an open or commercial market.
access_records.oversight_notes: Health Canada reviews each SAP request case by case. A subsection 56(1) class exemption lets practitioners, pharmacists, hospitals and licensed dealers handle SAP-authorized psilocybin; Health Canada states it will be revoked when new Controlled Substances Regulations take effect on 1 October 2026.
access_records.legal_basis: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act: production, sale and possession of psilocybin are illegal unless authorized by Health Canada. Psilocybin is a restricted drug obtainable for individual patients through the Special Access Program (serious or life-threatening conditions where conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable) or individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions. No approved psilocybin product.

MHLW is running clinical research so that patients with refractory epilepsy can continue using cannabis-derived products.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Refractory epilepsy patients through MHLW-funded clinical research; no general programme.
access_records.risk_notes: Criminal liability for unlawful possession and use.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Japan: no general medical cannabis access; limited clinical-research access for refractory epilepsy.
access_records.oversight_notes: MHLW; narcotics controls apply to cannabis.
access_records.legal_basis: Amended Cannabis Control Act / Narcotics and Psychotropics Control Act (first stage in force 12 Dec 2024): cannabis treated as a narcotic, unlawful use criminalised, ban on cannabis-derived medicines removed

access_records.procedure_name: Ozone Therapy for Infection / Inflammation / Wound Healing
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA regulation 21 CFR 801.415 states ozone is a toxic gas with no known useful medical application in specific, adjunctive, or preventive therapy; ozone-generating devices used for a medical condition without proof of safety and effectiveness are deemed adulterated and/or misbranded.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: No FDA-recognised medical ozone therapy pathway.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: no lawful FDA pathway for medical ozone generators (21 CFR 801.415).
access_records.oversight_notes: 21 CFR 801.415 treats medical-use ozone generators lacking proof of safety and effectiveness as adulterated/misbranded.
access_records.legal_basis: 21 CFR 801.415 (federal; applies in all states): ozone-generating devices used for a medical condition without proof of safety and effectiveness are adulterated and/or misbranded

sources.title: 21 CFR 801.415 Maximum acceptable level of ozone
sources.quote: Ozone is a toxic gas with no known useful medical application in specific, adjunctive, or preventive therapy.

sources.title: 21 CFR 801.415(c)
sources.quote: any such device will be considered adulterated and/or misbranded within the meaning of sections 501 and 502 of the act.

verification.notes: Federal rule applies in this state; no state statute creating an ozone pathway was checked. Stored template text (controlled-substance 'criminal liability for possession') did not fit and was removed. PROHIBITED rests on the device regulation; FDA does not regulate the practice of medicine itself. eCFR blocked; read via Cornell LII. No source rates oversight.

access_records.access_pathway_details: The Natural Medicine Health Act (Proposition 122, 2022), as amended by SB23-290, established regulated access to psilocybin for adults 21+ through licensed healing centers and licensed facilitators, and removed state penalties for personal possession, use, cultivation and sharing without remuneration. Business licence applications opened on 31 December 2024, and healing centers have since been licensed.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults 21 and older. Personal-use protections cover possession, use, cultivation and sharing without remuneration; they do not permit sale.
access_records.provider_requirements: Facilitators are licensed by the Division of Professions and Occupations (Department of Regulatory Agencies); healing centers and other natural medicine businesses are licensed by the Department of Revenue's Natural Medicine Division.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: State-regulated psilocybin services for adults 21+ through licensed healing centers and facilitators, alongside decriminalised personal possession, cultivation and sharing without remuneration. Psilocybin remains Schedule I under federal law.
access_records.oversight_notes: Two-agency regime: the Department of Revenue's Natural Medicine Division regulates natural medicine businesses including healing centers, cultivators, manufacturers and testers; the Division of Professions and Occupations licenses and regulates facilitators.
access_records.legal_basis: Natural Medicine Health Act of 2022 (Proposition 122, C.R.S. title 12 article 170), as amended by SB23-290: regulated access for adults 21+ to natural medicine (psilocybin) through licensed healing centers and facilitators; personal possession, use, cultivation and sharing without remuneration by adults 21+ is not a state offense. Psilocybin remains federally Schedule I.

access_records.procedure_name: Ketamine Infusion Therapy for Depression
access_records.access_pathway_details: IV ketamine for depression is off-label: ketamine is FDA-approved only as a general anaesthetic (Schedule III). Esketamine nasal spray (Spravato) is FDA-approved for treatment-resistant depression and is available only through the SPRAVATO REMS in certified healthcare settings.
access_records.risk_notes: Spravato labelling warns of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, and abuse and misuse; patients must be monitored for at least 2 hours after each dose. FDA has warned about compounded ketamine products used for psychiatric disorders.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Off-label IV ketamine under federal Schedule III rules; FDA-approved Spravato via REMS-certified settings.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal: ketamine is Schedule III (DEA); Spravato is subject to an FDA REMS. Off-label IV ketamine has no REMS.
access_records.legal_basis: Ketamine: FDA-approved general anaesthetic (Ketalar, NDA 016812), Schedule III under 21 CFR 1308.13(c)(7); not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder, so depression use is off-label. Esketamine (Spravato, NDA 211243) FDA-approved for TRD and MDD with acute suicidal ideation under the SPRAVATO REMS.

Esketamine (Spravato, NDA 211243) FDA-approved for TRD and MDD with acute suicidal ideation under the SPRAVATO REMS.

access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine (anaesthetic) and esketamine (SPRAVATO) are FDA-approved prescription drugs; ketamine for depression is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Ketamine (anaesthetic) and esketamine (SPRAVATO) are FDA-approved prescription drugs; ketamine for depression is off-label.

access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine medicines are used routinely in intensive care, ambulance care and veterinary medicine. Ketamine is not currently on an Opium Act list; in July 2026 the government said it was still considering whether to list it. Esketamine nasal spray (Spravato) holds an EU-wide marketing authorisation. IV ketamine for depression is off-label.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Netherlands: ketamine is an authorised medicine, not on the Opium Act lists (as of July 2026); depression use is off-label.

Spravato is centrally authorised in the EU since 18 Dec 2019.

access_records.access_pathway_details: Casgevy, the first FDA-approved CRISPR/Cas9 therapy, is approved federally and the approval applies in Oregon.

access_records.access_pathway_details: Zolgensma is FDA-approved and the federal approval applies in Oregon; it is given as a one-time infusion.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Pediatric patients under 2 years of age with SMA; liver function must be assessed before treatment and monitored for at least three months afterwards.
access_records.risk_notes: Acute serious liver injury can occur (US boxed warning); elevated liver enzymes/hepatotoxicity are among the most common side effects. Patients receive corticosteroids and liver and blood tests before and after the infusion.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: access follows the FDA approval; Zolgensma is prescribed for labeled SMA in children under 2.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-licensed biologic with a boxed warning for acute serious liver injury; liver function is monitored for at least three months after administration.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA biologics licence approval of Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi); first approval letter 24 May 2019.

access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. ZOLGENSMA (onasemnogene abeparvovec) is an FDA-approved gene therapy.

access_records.procedure_name: Mesenchymal Stem Cell (MSC) Therapy for Autoimmune/Inflammatory Conditions
access_records.access_pathway_details: Ryoncil (remestemcel-L), FDA-approved on 18 Dec 2024 for steroid-refractory acute GVHD in patients 2 months and older, is the first FDA-approved MSC therapy. Other MSC uses for autoimmune/inflammatory conditions need an FDA IND (clinical trial); cell products outside the 21 CFR 1271.10 criteria are regulated as biologics.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Outside Ryoncil's approved paediatric GVHD indication, access is through FDA-authorised clinical trials, with trial-specific eligibility.
access_records.provider_requirements: Approved product under prescription for the labelled indication; otherwise investigators under an FDA IND.
access_records.risk_notes: FDA reports receiving reports of blindness, tumor formation, infections and more from unapproved regenerative cell products.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: one approved MSC product (paediatric SR-aGVHD); other autoimmune/inflammatory uses through trials only.
access_records.oversight_notes: Regulated federally by FDA CBER.
access_records.legal_basis: PHS Act s.351 / 21 CFR 1271.10 and 1271.20 (more-than-minimally-manipulated or non-homologous cell products are regulated as biologics requiring BLA or IND); Ryoncil (remestemcel-L-rknd) BLA approval 18 Dec 2024

access_records.procedure_name: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) / Assisted Death
access_records.access_pathway_details: Euthanasia and assisted suicide are criminal offences except when performed by a physician who meets six statutory due care criteria under the Termination of Life on Request and Assisted Suicide (Review Procedures) Act.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: The physician must be satisfied that the request is voluntary and well considered and that suffering is unbearable with no prospect of improvement, must have informed the patient, and must have concluded with the patient that there is no reasonable alternative.
access_records.provider_requirements: Performed by a physician, who must consult at least one other independent physician who sees the patient and gives a written opinion, and must exercise due medical care.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Euthanasia and assisted suicide are lawful when a physician meets the statutory due care criteria, with case-by-case review by regional committees.
access_records.oversight_notes: Each case is reported to the municipal pathologist and assessed by one of five regional euthanasia review committees.
access_records.legal_basis: Termination of Life on Request and Assisted Suicide (Review Procedures) Act

access_records.procedure_name: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) / Assisted Death
access_records.access_pathway_details: Euthanasia is regulated by Organic Law 3/2021. A responsible physician certifies the condition and a consulting physician confirms the legal requirements; regional Guarantee and Evaluation Commissions review cases.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Spanish nationality or legal residence in Spain, or a registration certificate showing more than 12 months' stay; adult, capable and conscious at the time of request; serious and incurable illness or condition certified by the responsible physician.
access_records.provider_requirements: Responsible physician plus a consulting physician; health professionals may refuse on grounds of conscience, stated in advance and in writing.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: Requires Spanish nationality, legal residence, or more than 12 months' registered stay in Spain.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Euthanasia is legal and regulated, but limited to nationals, legal residents or people registered in Spain for over 12 months.
access_records.oversight_notes: Each autonomous community has a multidisciplinary Guarantee and Evaluation Commission (at least seven members) that resolves complaints and verifies within two months that the law was followed.
access_records.legal_basis: Ley Orgánica 3/2021, de 24 de marzo, de regulación de la eutanasia

access_records.procedure_name: Thymosin Alpha-1 (Thymalfasin) Immunomodulation
access_records.access_pathway_details: No FDA-approved drug product contains thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin). Compounded Ta1 products are marketed online in the US, but FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted in December 2024 against adding Ta1 to the 503A bulks list, and Ta1 is not among the bulk substances FDA lists as under evaluation.
access_records.provider_requirements: Under section 503A, a pharmacy may compound from a bulk substance only if it has a USP/NF monograph, is a component of an FDA-approved drug, or appears on FDA's 503A bulks list; FDA reviewed Ta1 and recommended against listing it.
access_records.risk_notes: FDA cited insufficient safety information, a lack of information on immunogenicity risk, and poor physicochemical characterisation of Ta1.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: no FDA-approved Ta1 product, and FDA has recommended against its use in 503A compounding.
access_records.legal_basis: FD&C Act §503A(b)(1)(A)(i) (21 U.S.C. 353a): Ta1 has no FDA-approved drug and is not on the 503A bulks list; PCAC voted 17-4 on 4 Dec 2024 against adding it; not in any 503A nomination category as of FDA's 14 May 2026 update

access_records.procedure_name: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) with Genetic Testing (PGT)
access_records.access_pathway_details: IVF is offered by fertility clinics, which must report data on the ART procedures they perform to CDC each year under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992. FDA regulates donated reproductive tissue (donor screening and infectious-disease testing).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: IVF with PGT is lawful; the federal framework consists of CDC outcome reporting and FDA rules for donated reproductive tissue.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal oversight centres on mandatory CDC reporting of ART cycles and FDA donor screening/testing rules for donated sperm, eggs and embryos. State-specific ART law was not reviewed for this record.
access_records.legal_basis: Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992 (CDC reporting); FDA donor screening and testing rules for reproductive tissue
access_records.regulatory_authority: CDC (ART outcome reporting) and FDA (donated reproductive tissue)

access_records.access_pathway_details: ART clinics must be accredited; compliance with the NHMRC ethical guidelines is a key element of accreditation. The guidelines prohibit non-medical sex selection and limit PGT to conditions that would severely limit the quality of life of the person who would be born. State/territory ART legislation applies where it exists.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Licensed (accredited) ART clinic regime; PGT for serious conditions; non-medical sex selection prohibited under NHMRC guidelines.
access_records.legal_basis: Research Involving Human Embryos Act 2002 (Cth) ss 8, 11 (mandatory accreditation); NHMRC Ethical guidelines on the use of ART (2017), incl. ¶8.14.1 sex selection
access_records.regulatory_authority: NHMRC (national ART ethical guidelines) with mandatory clinic accreditation (RTAC); state/territory ART laws where enacted

sources.title: Smith & Taylor-Sands, Comparing Non-Medical Sex Selection and Saviour Sibling Selection..., J Bioethical Inquiry 15(1) (2018)
sources.quote: compliance with them is a key element in the national accreditation system for state- and territory-based ART clinics in Australia ... these guidelines continue to prohibit non-medical sex selection in Australia (NHMRC 2017, ¶8.14.1)

sources.title: Smith & Taylor-Sands, J Bioethical Inquiry 15(1) (2018)
sources.quote: Accreditation is now mandatory under Commonwealth legislation regulating embryo research and human cloning (Research Involving Human Embryos Act, ss 8 and 11).

access_records.procedure_name: Gestational Surrogacy
access_records.access_pathway_details: Altruistic surrogacy is lawful under Chapter 19 of the Children's Act. The written agreement must be made in South Africa and confirmed by the High Court before it is valid.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: The commissioning parent(s) must be permanently and irreversibly unable to give birth. The surrogate must not use surrogacy as a source of income, must act for altruistic reasons, must have a documented history of at least one pregnancy and viable delivery, and must have a living child of her own.
access_records.provider_requirements: Prior High Court confirmation of the agreement is required.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: At least one commissioning parent (or a single commissioning parent) and the surrogate (and her partner) must be domiciled in South Africa when the agreement is made; a court may waive this on good cause.
access_records.cost_notes: Rewards or compensation are prohibited. Only expenses directly related to the pregnancy and birth, the surrogate's loss of earnings, and insurance may be paid, plus reasonable fees for bona fide legal and medical services.
access_records.legal_basis: Children's Act 38 of 2005, Chapter 19 (ss. 292–303)

access_records.access_pathway_details: Naltrexone hydrochloride is an FDA-approved prescription drug; low-dose use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.

access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Naltrexone hydrochloride is an FDA-approved prescription drug; low-dose use is off-label.

access_records.legal_basis: Naltrexone HCl 50 mg tablets were approved by CDSCO on 11-10-1996; legality of prescribing for unapproved indications is contested (secondary sources state Indian law does not permit it, citing 2002 Indian Medical Council regulations; no clear current guidelines).

sources.title: CDSCO, List of New Drugs Approved in India from 1991 to 2000, entry 212
sources.quote: 212 Naltrexone Hcl 50mg In the treatment of narcotic 11-10-1996 ... Uncoated Tablet antagonist and alcohol

sources.title: Ngcobo & Mathibe, Orphanet J Rare Dis 2024;19:448 (comparative section on India)
sources.quote: Under Indian law, prescribing drugs for unapproved indications is not permitted.

sources.title: BMJ 2004;328:974, Indian Medical Association wants off-label prescribing
sources.quote: Indian law does not currently allow drugs to be prescribed for indications for which they have not been approved.

sources.title: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019 (CDSCO consolidated), rule 2(w)(i)
sources.quote: a drug ... which has not been used in the country to any significant extent ... and has not been approved as safe and efficacious by the Central Licencing Authority with respect to its claims

verification.notes: Off-label status in India is legally unclear: Ngcobo & Mathibe 2024 and BMJ 2004 say off-label prescribing is not permitted, while the Drugs and Cosmetics Act/NDCT Rules regulate marketing rather than prescribing. Recorded as ambiguous/grey. Low-dose formulations would require dose splitting or compounding, not verified.

access_records.procedure_name: Methylene Blue (Pharmaceutical Grade) for Neuroprotection/Mitochondrial Dysfunction
access_records.access_pathway_details: Methylene blue injection (ProvayBlue) is FDA-approved, prescription only, for acquired methemoglobinemia; low-dose use for neuroprotection or mitochondrial dysfunction is off-label, which FDA says prescribers generally may do when medically appropriate (federal rule applies in all states).
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency; boxed warning against combination with serotonergic drugs and opioids.
access_records.provider_requirements: Prescription required (Rx only).
access_records.risk_notes: Boxed warning: serious or fatal serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs and opioids. Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (risk of hemolytic anemia).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: methylene blue is FDA-approved (ProvayBlue) for methemoglobinemia; neuroprotective use is off-label at prescriber discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-approved drug (methemoglobinemia); neuroprotective use is off-label.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approval of ProvayBlue (methylene blue injection), NDA 204630, for acquired methemoglobinemia; off-label prescribing of approved drugs at prescriber discretion per FDA

sources.title: Drugs@FDA: NDA 204630 PROVAYBLUE (methylene blue)
sources.quote: PROVAYBLUE | METHYLENE BLUE | SOLUTION;INTRAVENOUS | Prescription | NDA 204630 | PROVEPHARM SAS | approval 04/08/2016

sources.title: DailyMed: PROVAYBLUE (methylene blue injection) label
sources.quote: PROVAYBLUE is indicated for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with acquired methemoglobinemia. ... PROVAYBLUE may cause serious or fatal serotonergic syndrome when used in combination with serotonergic drugs and opioids.

sources.title: DailyMed: PROVAYBLUE (methylene blue injection) label
sources.quote: Contraindications: Patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (G6PD) due to the risk of hemolytic anemia

sources.title: FDA: Understanding Unapproved Use of Approved Drugs 'Off Label'
sources.quote: healthcare providers generally may prescribe the drug for an unapproved use when they judge that it is medically appropriate for their patient.

access_records.access_pathway_details: Methylene blue injection is an FDA-approved prescription drug; neuroprotective use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Methylene blue injection is an FDA-approved prescription drug; neuroprotective use is off-label.

access_records.procedure_name: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide / Tirzepatide) Beyond Diabetes
access_records.access_pathway_details: Semaglutide (OZEMPIC) and tirzepatide (ZEPBOUND) are FDA-approved prescription drugs. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Semaglutide (OZEMPIC) and tirzepatide (ZEPBOUND) are FDA-approved prescription drugs.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Próspera ZEDE Health Industry rules (reliance on Honduran or Best Practice Peer Country approvals, incl. US FDA)

access_records.procedure_name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) for Longevity/Healthspan
access_records.access_pathway_details: Sirolimus (Rapamune and generic tablets) is FDA-approved, prescription-only, for prophylaxis of organ rejection in renal transplant patients aged 13 and over and for lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM). Use for ageing/longevity is off-label and needs a prescription from a licensed prescriber.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: No regulatory eligibility criteria for off-label use; the prescriber judges whether it is medically appropriate for the patient.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (prescription-only drug). The label recommends therapeutic drug monitoring for all patients.
access_records.risk_notes: US label boxed warning: immunosuppression may increase susceptibility to infection and possible development of lymphoma and other malignancies. Label warnings include impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia, proteinuria, interstitial lung disease, embryo-fetal toxicity and male infertility; avoid strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors or inducers and live vaccines. Common adverse reactions in LAM patients include stomatitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and hypercholesterolemia. Labelled safety data come from transplant and LAM patients, not longevity dosing.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon (US federal rules): sirolimus is an FDA-approved generic prescription drug; prescribing it for longevity is lawful off-label use at the prescriber's discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA approves the drug and its labelling; FDA states that once a drug is approved, providers generally may prescribe it for an unapproved use when they judge it medically appropriate.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved prescription drug (Rapamune NDA 021083; generic sirolimus ANDAs) indicated for renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and LAM; longevity use is off-label, which FDA says providers generally may prescribe when medically appropriate

sources.quote: Rapamune is an mTOR inhibitor immunosuppressant indicated for the prophylaxis of organ rejection in patients aged ≥13 years receiving renal transplants ... Rapamune is an mTOR inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with lymphangioleiomyomatosis (1.3).

access_records.eligibility_requirements: No regulatory eligibility criteria for off-label use; the prescriber judges whether it is medically appropriate for the patient.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (prescription-only drug). The label recommends therapeutic drug monitoring for all patients.
access_records.risk_notes: US label boxed warning: immunosuppression may increase susceptibility to infection and possible development of lymphoma and other malignancies. Label warnings include impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia, proteinuria, interstitial lung disease, embryo-fetal toxicity and male infertility; avoid strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors or inducers and live vaccines. Common adverse reactions in LAM patients include stomatitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and hypercholesterolemia. Labelled safety data come from transplant and LAM patients, not longevity dosing.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Florida (US federal rules): sirolimus is an FDA-approved generic prescription drug; prescribing it for longevity is lawful off-label use at the prescriber's discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA approves the drug and its labelling; FDA states that once a drug is approved, providers generally may prescribe it for an unapproved use when they judge it medically appropriate.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved prescription drug (Rapamune NDA 021083; generic sirolimus ANDAs) indicated for renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and LAM; longevity use is off-label, which FDA says providers generally may prescribe when medically appropriate

access_records.access_pathway_details: Sirolimus (RAPAMUNE) is an FDA-approved prescription drug; longevity use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Sirolimus (RAPAMUNE) is an FDA-approved prescription drug; longevity use is off-label.

access_records.arbitrage_summary: Netherlands: sirolimus is an authorised prescription medicine; longevity use would be off-label prescribing, subject to the national conditions noted.
access_records.oversight_notes: Authorised centrally by the European Commission on EMA advice; national competent authority: College ter Beoordeling van Geneesmiddelen (MEB/CBG); inspection by IGJ. EU legislation does not regulate how authorised medicines are used in medical practice; off-label prescribing is a national/professional matter.

access_records.procedure_name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) for Longevity/Healthspan
access_records.access_pathway_details: Sirolimus (Rapamune) holds an EU-wide marketing authorisation valid in France; it is prescription-only and indicated for renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis. Use for ageing/longevity is off-label.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Under the French public health code (art. L.5121-12-1, as summarised by the Ordre des médecins), prescribing outside the marketing authorisation is permitted in the absence of an appropriate authorised medicine for the patient's condition.
access_records.provider_requirements: Prescription from a licensed prescriber.
access_records.risk_notes: Product labelling warns that immunosuppression may increase susceptibility to infection and possible development of lymphoma and other malignancies; other labelled risks include impaired wound healing, hyperlipidemia and proteinuria. Labelled safety data come from transplant and LAM patients, not longevity dosing.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: France: sirolimus is an authorised prescription medicine; longevity use would be off-label prescribing, subject to the national conditions noted.
access_records.oversight_notes: Authorised centrally by the European Commission on EMA advice; national competent authority: ANSM. EU legislation does not regulate how authorised medicines are used in medical practice; off-label prescribing is a national/professional matter.
access_records.legal_basis: Rapamune EU marketing authorisation (14 March 2001), valid in all EU member states; off-label use not regulated by EU law; Code de la santé publique art. L.5121-12-1 (conditional off-label prescribing)

access_records.access_pathway_details: No CDSCO-approved exosome product was found; stem-cell-derived products are regulated as new drugs and unproven stem-cell therapies may be offered only within approved, monitored clinical trials.
access_records.risk_notes: Offering unapproved stem-cell therapy can lead to cancellation of clinic registration and fines under the Clinical Establishments Act 2010 and professional-misconduct action.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: India: stem-cell-derived products are new drugs; outside approved trials their therapeutic use is treated as malpractice.
access_records.legal_basis: Cell or stem-cell derived products are 'new drugs' under NDCT Rules 2019 r 2(w)(v) requiring CDSCO permission (r 74); ICMR 2017 guidelines treat stem-cell use outside approved trials as malpractice; Supreme Court (2026 INSC 96) and a Sept 2026 Health Ministry advisory confine unproven stem-cell therapy to approved trials.

access_records.procedure_name: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Chronic Wounds/TBI/Lyme
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA has cleared hyperbaric chambers for specific conditions and warns that some centres promote uncleared uses such as Lyme disease. Medicare covers HBO for listed conditions, including qualifying diabetic wounds of the lower extremities.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: HBOT for qualifying diabetic wounds is an FDA-cleared, Medicare-covered use; Lyme disease is not a cleared use. No state-specific rule was searched.
access_records.legal_basis: 21 CFR 868.5470 (hyperbaric chamber, Class II); Medicare NCD 20.29 Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (device clearance, 21 CFR 868.5470); CMS (Medicare coverage, NCD 20.29)

sources.title: FDA bulletin 26 Jul 2021: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy: Get the Facts
sources.quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the use of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) for the treatment of several conditions.

sources.quote: promoting hyperbaric oxygen chambers for uses that have not been cleared or approved by the FDA, such as treatment of cancer, Lyme disease, autism, or Alzheimer's disease.

sources.quote: the FDA advises you get the treatment at a hospital or facility that has been inspected and is accredited by the Undersea and Hyperbaric Medical Society.

sources.title: 21 CFR 868.5470 Hyperbaric chamber
sources.quote: Classification. Class II (performance standards).

sources.title: CMS National Coverage Determination 20.29 Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy
sources.quote: 12/27/2002 - Expanded coverage for treatment of diabetic wounds of the lower extremities in patients that meet three criteria.

sources.title: CMS NCD 20.29 Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (continuation / supervision)
sources.quote: Continued treatment with HBO therapy is not covered if measurable signs of healing have not been demonstrated within any 30-day period of treatment.

access_records.procedure_name: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) for CDI/IBD
access_records.access_pathway_details: Australia has a registered FMT product (Biomictra). Its conditions of registration restrict release to C. difficile infection; use for other conditions (e.g. IBD) is possible only in a registered clinical trial or via the Special Access Scheme or Authorised Prescriber Scheme.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: C. difficile infection under the registered product; other indications only via trial, SAS or Authorised Prescriber.
access_records.provider_requirements: Registered medical practitioner, under the supervision or on the advice of a specialist gastroenterologist or infectious diseases physician.
access_records.legal_basis: TGA registration of Biomictra (faecal microbiota, BiomeBank) as a biological on the ARTG, with conditions of registration limiting release to C. difficile infection except via registered clinical trial, Special Access Scheme or Authorised Prescriber Scheme

access_records.procedure_name: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) for CDI/IBD
access_records.access_pathway_details: Health Canada regulates FMT as a new biologic drug with no market authorization, so it is investigational and normally limited to authorized clinical trials. An interim policy lets health care practitioners use FMT to treat C. difficile infection outside a trial if the guidance conditions are followed.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: C. difficile infection under the interim policy (the only indication covered); other indications only in authorized clinical trials.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: FMT for C. difficile is available under a Health Canada interim policy; other uses are trial-only.
access_records.legal_basis: Food and Drugs Act; Health Canada guidance 'Regulation of FMT for treatment of C. difficile infections not responsive to conventional therapies' (effective 27 Mar 2015, revised 26 Sep 2022)

access_records.procedure_name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide) for Sexual Dysfunction
access_records.access_pathway_details: Vyleesi (bremelanotide) is FDA-approved and prescribed under the same federal rules as elsewhere in the US.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: FDA label: premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD); not for postmenopausal women or men. Contraindicated in uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease.
access_records.risk_notes: Most common adverse reactions are nausea, flushing, injection-site reactions, headache and vomiting; blood pressure rises and heart rate falls transiently after each dose.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Same FDA-approved status as the US federal record.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approval of Vyleesi (bremelanotide) injection, NDA 210557, 21 June 2019; pharmacy compounding governed by FD&C Act s.503A (21 U.S.C. 353a)

access_records.procedure_name: Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) Therapy for Joint/Tissue Repair
access_records.access_pathway_details: Most PRP preparation systems are FDA 510(k)-cleared for producing PRP to be mixed with bone graft material in orthopedic practice; office injection of PRP outside that setting is off-label use of the device. As a blood product, PRP itself is exempt from the traditional FDA regulatory pathway.
access_records.risk_notes: Insurer medical policy (FEP Blue, 2026) considers PRP investigational for all orthopedic indications.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA 510(k) device clearance (bone-graft handling indication); off-label use of legally marketed devices preserved by 21 U.S.C. § 396
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (510(k) clearance of PRP preparation devices); PRP itself exempt from traditional FDA pathway

sources.title: FEP Blue Medical Policy 2.01.98 Orthopedic Applications of Platelet-Rich Plasma (July 2026)
sources.quote: certain products including blood products such as platelet-rich plasma are exempt and therefore do not follow the traditional FDA regulatory pathway. ... The use of platelet-rich plasma outside of this setting (eg, an office injection) would be considered off-label.

sources.title: FEP Blue Medical Policy 2.01.98 Orthopedic Applications of Platelet-Rich Plasma (July 2026)
sources.quote: many of which were cleared for marketing by the FDA through the 510(k) process for producing platelet-rich preparations intended to be mixed with bone graft materials to enhance the bone grafting properties in orthopedic practices.

sources.title: 21 U.S.C. § 396 – Practice of medicine
sources.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to limit or interfere with the authority of a health care practitioner to prescribe or administer any legally marketed device to a patient for any condition or disease

sources.title: FEP Blue Medical Policy 2.01.98 Orthopedic Applications of Platelet-Rich Plasma (July 2026)
sources.quote: Use of platelet-rich plasma is considered investigational for all orthopedic indications.

verification.notes: No PRP-specific state statute identified; status follows federal device regime. Stored values for this inferred cell were generic 'wellness infusion' defaults (MEDICAL_TOURISM_CASH, IV competency, psilocybin regulators) not applicable to PRP. State medical-board rules not separately verified; no state-specific price source.

access_records.arbitrage_summary: Minimally manipulated autologous PRP is an approved, DHA-licensed clinical service in Dubai.
