access_records.procedure_name: NMN/NR Oral Supplementation for Longevity
access_records.access_pathway_details: NR is sold as a dietary supplement (nicotinamide riboside chloride GRAS notice GRN 635, FDA 'no questions'). FDA excluded NMN from the dietary-supplement definition in 2022 because it had been investigated as a drug, but letters dated 29 September 2025 confirmed NMN is not excluded, so NMN is again lawful in dietary supplements.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Consumer purchase as a dietary supplement under federal law.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Federal law governs: NR and NMN are both lawfully sold as dietary supplements (NMN since FDA's September 2025 reversal).
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA's 2022 drug-preclusion exclusion of NMN was reversed in September 2025; NMN is now treated as lawful in dietary supplements.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA responses of 29 Sept 2025 to NMN citizen petitions (NMN not excluded from the dietary-supplement definition, reversing FDA's 2022 position); nicotinamide riboside chloride GRAS Notice GRN 635 (FDA 'no questions', 2016)

access_records.procedure_name: Ozone Therapy for Infection / Inflammation / Wound Healing
access_records.access_pathway_details: Lei 14.648/2023 authorises ozone therapy as a complementary procedure, only by university-level health professionals registered with their council, using ANVISA-regularised medical ozone equipment; patients must be told it is complementary. ANVISA's Nota Técnica 41/2026 recognises adjuvant use for diabetic-foot ulcers and acute infected wounds in adults.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults (18+) for ANVISA-recognised wound indications; the patient must be informed the procedure is complementary.
access_records.provider_requirements: University-level health professional registered with their professional council, using ANVISA-regularised ozone equipment.
access_records.risk_notes: ANVISA states ozone therapy does not replace conventional treatment and should be used only as an adjuvant within approved indications.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Brazil: ozone therapy authorised by federal law as a complementary procedure; ANVISA recognises adjuvant wound-care use.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal statute plus ANVISA device regularisation and indication notes (Nota Técnica 41/2026).
access_records.legal_basis: Lei nº 14.648/2023 (authorises ozone therapy as a complementary procedure); ANVISA Nota Técnica nº 41/2026 (adjuvant use for diabetic-foot ulcers and acute infected wounds in adults)
access_records.regulatory_authority: ANVISA (device regularisation); practitioners registered with their professional council

access_records.eligibility_requirements: Trial inclusion criteria.
access_records.provider_requirements: Investigators under an FDA-cleared IND.
access_records.risk_notes: FDA has received reports of blindness, tumor formation and infections from unapproved regenerative products.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Clinical trials only for neural stem cell therapy; no state law creates a lawful commercial route for neurological indications.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA (CBER) rules on cell products apply in every state.
access_records.legal_basis: PHS Act s.351 / 21 CFR Part 1271: cell products that are not minimally manipulated or not for homologous use require an FDA BLA, or an IND for investigational use

access_records.access_pathway_details: Dasatinib is an FDA-approved prescription drug labelled for Philadelphia chromosome-positive leukaemias; use with quercetin as a senolytic is off-label.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: No regulatory eligibility criteria for off-label use; the prescriber judges medical appropriateness.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (dasatinib is prescription-only).
access_records.risk_notes: Dasatinib label warns of myelosuppression and bleeding-related events.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: same federal position as the rest of the US: off-label prescribing of dasatinib only.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA rules apply; no state-specific rule on senolytic use identified.
access_records.legal_basis: Dasatinib (Sprycel, NDA 021986) is FDA-approved for Ph+ leukaemias; senolytic use is off-label, which FDA states providers generally may prescribe when medically appropriate. No state-specific statute on D+Q identified.
access_records.regulatory_authority: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA); state medical board licenses prescribers

access_records.procedure_name: Senolytic Therapy (Dasatinib + Quercetin) for Cellular Aging
access_records.access_pathway_details: Dasatinib is an FDA-approved prescription drug; senolytic use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Dasatinib is an FDA-approved prescription drug; senolytic use is off-label.

access_records.procedure_name: Metformin for Longevity / Aging Prevention
access_records.access_pathway_details: Metformin is in FDA-approved prescription products; longevity use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Metformin is in FDA-approved prescription products; longevity use is off-label.

access_records.procedure_name: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) for Parkinson's Disease
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA premarket approval of DBS systems for Parkinson's disease applies nationally, including in this state. Medicare covers STN or GPi DBS for Parkinson's disease when national coverage criteria are met.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Medicare criteria include advanced idiopathic Parkinson's disease, levodopa responsiveness with clearly defined 'on' periods, and persistent disabling symptoms or drug side effects.
access_records.risk_notes: Reported complications include risk of stroke, confusion, speech disorders and visual problems.
access_records.oversight_notes: DBS systems for Parkinson's disease reach the US market through FDA premarket approval (PMA); Medicare coverage follows a national coverage determination.

access_records.procedure_name: Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) Therapy for Melanoma
access_records.estimated_cost_range_usd: $515,000 product list price (WAC, 2024 launch); hospital costs extra
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA-approved Amtagvi (lifileucel) is given at authorized treatment centers in an inpatient hospital setting.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults with unresectable or metastatic melanoma previously treated with a PD-1 blocking antibody and, if BRAF V600-positive, a BRAF inhibitor with or without a MEK inhibitor; tumour tissue is removed surgically to manufacture the product.
access_records.provider_requirements: Authorized treatment centers; inpatient hospital with an intensive care facility and specialists skilled in cardiopulmonary or intensive care medicine available.
access_records.risk_notes: Boxed warning for treatment-related mortality, prolonged severe cytopenia, severe infection, and cardiopulmonary and renal impairment; the regimen includes lymphodepleting chemotherapy before and interleukin-2 after the infusion.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Federal FDA approval applies in this state; treatment only at authorized treatment centers.
access_records.oversight_notes: No REMS; the label requires administration in an inpatient hospital setting with an intensive care facility available. Approved under accelerated approval; a confirmatory trial is ongoing.
access_records.cost_notes: US list price (WAC) $515,000 at launch; Iovance expected payer coverage similar to CAR T therapies.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA biologics licence approval of Amtagvi (lifileucel), 16 Feb 2024, under accelerated approval (confirmatory trial ongoing); federal approval applies in every state
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research)

access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults with unresectable or metastatic melanoma previously treated with a PD-1 blocking antibody and, if BRAF V600-positive, a BRAF inhibitor with or without a MEK inhibitor; tumour tissue is removed surgically to manufacture the product.
access_records.provider_requirements: Authorized treatment centers; inpatient hospital with an intensive care facility and specialists skilled in cardiopulmonary or intensive care medicine available.
access_records.risk_notes: Boxed warning for treatment-related mortality, prolonged severe cytopenia, severe infection, and cardiopulmonary and renal impairment; the regimen includes lymphodepleting chemotherapy before and interleukin-2 after the infusion.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Federal FDA approval applies in this state; treatment only at authorized treatment centers.
access_records.oversight_notes: No REMS; the label requires administration in an inpatient hospital setting with an intensive care facility available. Approved under accelerated approval; a confirmatory trial is ongoing.
access_records.cost_notes: US list price (WAC) $515,000 at launch; Iovance expected payer coverage similar to CAR T therapies.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA biologics licence approval of Amtagvi (lifileucel), 16 Feb 2024, under accelerated approval (confirmatory trial ongoing); federal approval applies in every state
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research)

access_records.procedure_name: Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) Therapy for Melanoma
access_records.access_pathway_details: Academic TIL therapy produced by the NKI or Sanquin is given under a hospital exemption approved by the IGJ and has been covered by basic health insurance since January 2023; Amtagvi has no EU marketing authorisation.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: People with metastatic melanoma who cannot have surgery and who did not respond to immunotherapy.
access_records.provider_requirements: Hospital-exemption product made in the Netherlands by the NKI or Sanquin.
access_records.risk_notes: Lymphodepleting chemotherapy before and interleukin-2 after the infusion; serious side effects have been reported with TIL regimens.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Netherlands: reimbursed academic TIL under a hospital exemption, ahead of any EU-authorised product.
access_records.oversight_notes: IGJ hospital-exemption approval; reimbursement decision by Zorginstituut Nederland (December 2022).
access_records.cost_notes: Covered by Dutch basic health insurance for eligible patients.
access_records.legal_basis: Hospital exemption (ATMP Regulation (EC) 1394/2007 art. 28) granted by IGJ for TIL produced by NKI or Sanquin; Zorginstituut basic-package coverage from 15 Jan 2023; no EU marketing authorisation (EMA application withdrawn 22 Jul 2025)
access_records.regulatory_authority: IGJ (hospital exemption); Zorginstituut Nederland (reimbursement); EMA for any EU marketing authorisation

access_records.procedure_name: Experimental CAR-T / TCR Therapy for Solid Tumors
access_records.access_pathway_details: Solid-tumour CAR-T/TCR cell therapies are advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs). In the EU, ATMPs may be supplied legally only if centrally authorised via EMA, given in a clinical trial authorised by a national authority, or used in a hospital under a national hospital exemption; Netherlands has a national hospital-exemption framework. The IGJ decides on hospital-exemption applications; preparation for up to 10 patients per year counts as made to order for a specific patient.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Clinical-trial criteria, or an individual patient's medical prescription for a custom-made product under the hospital exemption.
access_records.provider_requirements: Hospital-exemption products are prepared on a non-routine basis to specific quality standards and used in a hospital under the exclusive professional responsibility of a medical practitioner.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: Hospital-exemption products must be used in a hospital within the same Member State.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Netherlands: solid-tumour CAR-T/TCR only via authorised clinical trials or the national hospital exemption.
access_records.legal_basis: Geneesmiddelenwet art. 40(3)(d) (hospital exemption); Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007
access_records.regulatory_authority: IGJ (Health and Youth Care Inspectorate) decides hospital-exemption applications; central authorisation via EMA

access_records.procedure_name: Dendritic Cell Cancer Vaccines (Personalized)
access_records.estimated_cost_range_usd: ~$93,000 per 3-infusion Provenge course (2011 list price; current price not verified)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Sipuleucel-T (Provenge), an autologous cellular immunotherapy, is FDA-licensed for asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer. Other personalized dendritic cell vaccines are investigational in the US and are available through clinical trials or FDA expanded access.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Provenge: asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (FDA label). Other DC vaccines: trial or expanded-access criteria.
access_records.provider_requirements: Provenge is administered by urologists or oncologists who offer it; the labeled course is 3 doses at approximately 2-week intervals.
access_records.risk_notes: Provenge label warns of acute infusion reactions within 1 day of infusion (e.g. nausea, vomiting, fatigue, fever).
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: one FDA-licensed dendritic-cell-based vaccine (Provenge, prostate cancer); other personalized DC vaccines are investigational.
access_records.cost_notes: Medicare covers on-label Provenge under a 2011 CMS national coverage decision.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA biologics licence for sipuleucel-T (Provenge) for metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer; other personalized DC vaccines are investigational (FDA clinical trials or expanded access; federal Right to Try for eligible investigational products)

access_records.procedure_name: Dendritic Cell Cancer Vaccines (Personalized)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Personalized dendritic cell vaccines are advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs). In the EU, ATMPs may be supplied legally only if centrally authorised via EMA, given in a clinical trial authorised by a national authority, or used in a hospital under a national hospital exemption; Netherlands has a national hospital-exemption framework. Provenge's EU marketing authorisation was withdrawn in 2015. The IGJ decides on hospital-exemption applications; preparation for up to 10 patients per year counts as made to order for a specific patient.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Clinical-trial criteria, or an individual patient's medical prescription for a custom-made product under the hospital exemption.
access_records.provider_requirements: Hospital-exemption products are prepared on a non-routine basis to specific quality standards and used in a hospital under the exclusive professional responsibility of a medical practitioner.
access_records.residency_travel_notes: Hospital-exemption products must be used in a hospital within the same Member State.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Netherlands: DC vaccines only via authorised clinical trials or the national hospital exemption.
access_records.oversight_notes: EMA and the Heads of Medicines Agencies warned in March 2025 that some unregulated products in the EU are sold as dendritic cell therapies for cancer.
access_records.legal_basis: Geneesmiddelenwet art. 40(3)(d) (hospital exemption); Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007
access_records.regulatory_authority: IGJ (Health and Youth Care Inspectorate) decides hospital-exemption applications; central authorisation via EMA

access_records.procedure_name: Therapeutic Apheresis / HELP Apheresis for Long COVID & Microclot Protocols
access_records.access_pathway_details: Therapeutic blood cell/plasma separators are a legally marketed (pre-amendment) FDA device type; using them for long COVID would be off-label, which federal law does not prohibit physicians from doing.
access_records.risk_notes: A phase II double-blind randomized trial (Nature Communications 2025) of six sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange vs sham in 50 people with post-COVID condition found no difference between groups in any efficacy parameter.
access_records.legal_basis: No FDA-cleared long-COVID indication identified for apheresis; physician use of legally marketed devices for any condition preserved by 21 U.S.C. § 396

access_records.procedure_name: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) for Autoimmune / Neuroimmune Disease
access_records.access_pathway_details: Federal FDA licensure applies: IGIV products such as Privigen are licensed for chronic ITP and CIDP (and primary immunodeficiency); other autoimmune/neuroimmune uses are off-label.
access_records.risk_notes: FDA boxed warning: thrombosis, renal dysfunction and acute renal failure.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: IVIG available on prescription under FDA licensure for labeled autoimmune indications (e.g. ITP, CIDP).
access_records.legal_basis: FDA biologics licences for IGIV products, e.g. PRIVIGEN BLA125201 (chronic ITP, CIDP)

access_records.procedure_name: SGLT2 Inhibitors for Heart Failure & CKD Beyond Diabetes
access_records.access_pathway_details: Dapagliflozin (Farxiga) and empagliflozin (Jardiance) are FDA-approved, prescription-only, for adults with heart failure and for adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression, independent of diabetes.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Adults with heart failure, or with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression, per the labels. The labels say they are not recommended for CKD in polycystic kidney disease or in patients requiring or recently on immunosuppressive therapy for kidney disease.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (prescription-only drugs).
access_records.risk_notes: Label warnings include ketoacidosis, volume depletion, genitourinary infections (including urosepsis, Fournier's gangrene and genital mycotic infections) and hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or insulin secretagogues.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon (US federal rules): dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are FDA-approved for heart failure and CKD in adults with or without diabetes, so this is on-label prescribing.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-approved labelling (Farxiga NDA 202293; Jardiance NDA 204629).
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved labels: FARXIGA (dapagliflozin) NDA 202293 and JARDIANCE (empagliflozin) NDA 204629 include heart-failure and chronic-kidney-disease indications in adults

sources.title: FARXIGA (dapagliflozin) US Prescribing Information (Drugs@FDA NDA 202293, SUPPL-35, 06/2026)
sources.quote: To reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end stage kidney disease, cardiovascular (CV) death, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression. ... To reduce the risk of CV death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent heart failure visit in adults with heart failure.

sources.title: JARDIANCE (empagliflozin) US Prescribing Information (Drugs@FDA NDA 204629, SUPPL-63, 10/2025)
sources.quote: To reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with heart failure. ... To reduce the risk of sustained decline in eGFR, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization in adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of progression.

sources.title: FARXIGA US Prescribing Information, Highlights: limitations of use
sources.quote: Not recommended for the treatment of chronic kidney disease in patients with polycystic kidney disease or patients requiring or with a recent history of immunosuppressive therapy for the treatment of kidney disease.

sources.title: openFDA Drugs@FDA record NDA202293 (FARXIGA)
sources.quote: "application_number": "NDA202293" "sponsor_name": "ASTRAZENECA AB" "brand_name": "FARXIGA" "marketing_status": "Prescription"

sources.title: FARXIGA US Prescribing Information, Highlights: warnings and precautions
sources.quote: Genitourinary Infections, including Urosepsis, Pyelonephritis, Necrotizing Fasciitis of the Perineum (Fournier’s Gangrene), and Genital Mycotic Infections

sources.title: JARDIANCE US Prescribing Information, Highlights: warnings and precautions
sources.quote: Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and Other Ketoacidosis: Consider ketone monitoring in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus and consider ketone monitoring in others at risk for ketoacidosis

sources.title: FARXIGA US Prescribing Information, Highlights: warnings and precautions
sources.quote: Volume depletion: Before initiating FARXIGA, assess volume status and renal function in the elderly, patients with renal impairment or low systolic blood pressure, and in patients on diuretics.

sources.title: FARXIGA US Prescribing Information, Highlights: warnings and precautions
sources.quote: Hypoglycemia: Consider a lower dose of insulin or the insulin secretagogue to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia when used in combination with FARXIGA.

verification.notes: Stored APPROVED_OFF_LABEL/OFF_LABEL_PRESCRIPTION corrected: HF and CKD are labelled indications. Oversight rating not evidenced; costs unsourced (brand price range not verified).

access_records.access_pathway_details: Empagliflozin (JARDIANCE) is an FDA-approved prescription drug. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Empagliflozin (JARDIANCE) is an FDA-approved prescription drug.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Próspera ZEDE Health Industry rules (reliance on Honduran or Best Practice Peer Country approvals, incl. US FDA)

access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA approval applies in every state: Wegovy (semaglutide) is labelled for weight reduction, cardiovascular risk reduction and MASH; Zepbound (tirzepatide) for weight reduction and obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity. FDA states that healthcare providers generally may prescribe an approved drug for an unapproved use.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: semaglutide/tirzepatide are authorised for other indications; use for alcohol or substance use disorder is off-label at the prescriber's discretion.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA declared the semaglutide injection shortage resolved (21 Feb 2025) and ended shortage-based enforcement discretion for compounders; on 30 Apr 2026 it proposed excluding semaglutide and tirzepatide from the 503B bulks list.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved semaglutide/tirzepatide products (no alcohol/substance use disorder indication); off-label prescribing permitted under FDA policy

Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Semaglutide (OZEMPIC) and tirzepatide (ZEPBOUND) are FDA-approved prescription drugs.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Próspera ZEDE Health Industry rules (reliance on Honduran or Best Practice Peer Country approvals, incl. US FDA)

access_records.procedure_name: Prazosin for PTSD Nightmares
access_records.access_pathway_details: Prazosin is an FDA-approved prescription drug (generic capsules) labelled for hypertension; use for PTSD-associated nightmares is off-label. The 2023 VA/DoD PTSD guideline suggests prazosin for nightmares associated with PTSD (weak recommendation) but suggests against it for PTSD overall.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: No regulatory eligibility criteria for off-label use; the prescriber judges medical appropriateness.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed prescriber (prescription-only drug).
access_records.risk_notes: Label warns prazosin may cause syncope with sudden loss of consciousness, usually within 30-90 minutes of the initial dose; therapy should start at 1 mg.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: same as federal; generic prazosin may be prescribed off-label for PTSD nightmares.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA rules govern: prazosin is approved for hypertension and its use for PTSD nightmares is off-label.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved prescription drug (Minipress NDA 017442 and generic prazosin HCl capsules) indicated for hypertension; prescribing for PTSD-associated nightmares is off-label use, which FDA states providers generally may do when medically appropriate

access_records.procedure_name: Prazosin for PTSD Nightmares
access_records.access_pathway_details: Prazosin (MINIPRESS) is an FDA-approved prescription drug; PTSD-nightmare use is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Prazosin (MINIPRESS) is an FDA-approved prescription drug; PTSD-nightmare use is off-label.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Próspera ZEDE Health Industry rules (reliance on Honduran or Best Practice Peer Country approvals, incl. US FDA)

access_records.procedure_name: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) for HIV Lipodystrophy / Off-Label Visceral Fat
access_records.access_pathway_details: Egrifta (tesamorelin) is FDA-approved and prescribed under the same federal rules as elsewhere in the US; compounding exemptions do not cover it because it is a licensed biological product.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: FDA label: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat; contraindicated with disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, active malignancy, or pregnancy.
access_records.risk_notes: Label warnings include glucose intolerance or diabetes, raised IGF-1, fluid retention and hypersensitivity; common reactions include arthralgia, injection-site erythema and peripheral oedema.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Same FDA-approved status as the US federal record.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA-licensed biological product (deemed a BLA since March 2020); the FD&C Act s.503A/503B compounding exemptions do not cover biological products.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA approval of Egrifta (tesamorelin), application 022505, 10 Nov 2010; deemed a biologics licence (BLA) under the BPCI Act on 23 March 2020

sources.title: Drugs@FDA: BLA 022505 EGRIFTA (tesamorelin acetate)
sources.quote: EGRIFTA ... TESAMORELIN ACETATE ... Prescription ... Company: THERATECHNOLOGIES [original approval 11/10/2010; latest label 03/25/2025, SUPPL-20]

sources.title: EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (rev. 3/2025)
sources.quote: EGRIFTA WR is a growth hormone-releasing factor (GHRF) analog indicated for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adult patients with lipodystrophy.

sources.title: EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (rev. 3/2025)
sources.quote: Patients with disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis (4) Patients with active malignancy (4) ... Pregnancy (4)

sources.title: EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (rev. 3/2025)
sources.quote: Glucose intolerance or diabetes mellitus: May develop with EGRIFTA WR use. Evaluate glucose prior to and during therapy.

sources.title: EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (rev. 3/2025)
sources.quote: Most commonly reported adverse reactions (>5%): Arthralgia, injection site erythema, injection site pruritus, pain in extremity, peripheral edema, and myalgia.

access_records.procedure_name: Elective Oocyte Cryopreservation (Social Egg Freezing)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Elective (non-medical) egg freezing is offered as a self-pay or insurance-covered procedure at US fertility clinics. It is lawful medical practice, not a product approval.
access_records.risk_notes: Ovarian stimulation can rarely cause ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). Freezing eggs does not guarantee a future pregnancy.
access_records.oversight_notes: Clinics performing ART must report cycle data to CDC under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992. FDA rules for human cells and tissues (21 CFR 1271) apply, with autologous use exempt from donor-eligibility screening.
access_records.legal_basis: No state statute specific to elective oocyte cryopreservation was found. Federal framework: Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act of 1992; 21 CFR Part 1271.
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (HCT/P rules, 21 CFR 1271); CDC (ART reporting); state medical board

access_records.procedure_name: Elective Oocyte Cryopreservation (Social Egg Freezing)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Since the 2021 bioethics law, women may freeze their eggs without a medical reason at authorised assisted-reproduction (AMP) centres.

access_records.provider_requirements: Only authorised AMP centres may perform it. The Agence de la biomédecine publishes the list.
access_records.risk_notes: Complications are rare but can arise from anaesthesia, retrieval (infection, haemorrhage) or stimulation (hyperstimulation, ovarian torsion). Freezing does not guarantee a later pregnancy.
access_records.oversight_notes: Governed by the 2021 bioethics law. Agence de la biomédecine oversight.
access_records.legal_basis: Loi n° 2021-1017 du 2 août 2021 relative à la bioéthique (autoconservation de gamètes, Code de la santé publique)
access_records.regulatory_authority: Agence de la biomédecine (with authorised AMP centres)

access_records.procedure_name: Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy uses ketamine off-label: ketamine is FDA-approved only as a general anaesthetic (Schedule III) and is not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder. Esketamine (Spravato) is a separate FDA-approved product available only through the SPRAVATO REMS.
access_records.risk_notes: Spravato labelling warns of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, and abuse and misuse; patients must be monitored for at least 2 hours after each dose. FDA has warned about compounded ketamine products used for psychiatric disorders.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: US: KAP relies on off-label ketamine under federal Schedule III rules.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal: ketamine is Schedule III (DEA); Spravato is subject to an FDA REMS. Off-label IV ketamine has no REMS.
access_records.legal_basis: Ketamine: FDA-approved general anaesthetic (Ketalar, NDA 016812), Schedule III under 21 CFR 1308.13(c)(7); not FDA-approved for any psychiatric disorder, so depression use is off-label. Esketamine (Spravato, NDA 211243) FDA-approved for TRD and MDD with acute suicidal ideation under the SPRAVATO REMS.
access_records.regulatory_authority: FDA (drug approval); DEA (Controlled Substances Act scheduling)

access_records.procedure_name: Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine (anaesthetic) and esketamine (SPRAVATO) are FDA-approved prescription drugs; ketamine for depression is off-label. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Ketamine (anaesthetic) and esketamine (SPRAVATO) are FDA-approved prescription drugs; ketamine for depression is off-label.
access_records.regulatory_authority: Próspera ZEDE Health Industry rules (reliance on Honduran or Best Practice Peer Country approvals, incl. US FDA)

access_records.access_pathway_details: Ketamine-assisted psychotherapy relies on off-label prescribing of ketamine. Philippine FDA registration of specific products and of esketamine was not verified.

access_records.procedure_name: Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA has granted premarket approval to Medtronic PulseSelect (December 2023), Boston Scientific FARAPULSE (January 2024; persistent AF added by a later supplement) and Biosense Webster VARIPULSE (November 2024) pulsed field ablation systems for atrial fibrillation.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: FDA-approved indications include drug-refractory, recurrent, symptomatic paroxysmal AF (FARAPULSE, PulseSelect) and persistent AF with episodes under one year (PulseSelect; FARAPULSE via supplement).
access_records.risk_notes: FDA's safety summary for FARAPULSE lists potential adverse effects including cardiac arrest, death, hypotension, hemolysis, conduction pathway injury, phrenic nerve injury and vessel perforation.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: FDA-approved PFA systems apply nationwide.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA premarket approval governs the devices.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA premarket approval (PMA): PulseSelect P230017 (12/13/2023), FARAPULSE P230030 (01/30/2024; persistent AF added by supplement S007), VARIPULSE P240006 (11/06/2024)

access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Lecanemab (LEQEMBI) and donanemab (KISUNLA) are FDA-approved prescription biologics.

access_records.procedure_name: Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT) for Hypogonadism
access_records.access_pathway_details: TRT for diagnosed hypogonadism is an on-label use of FDA-approved testosterone products, which are federally Schedule III controlled substances.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Label indication is hypogonadism due to identified conditions; safety and efficacy in age-related hypogonadism not established.
access_records.provider_requirements: Licensed, DEA-registered prescriber (Schedule III).
access_records.risk_notes: Labels warn of polycythemia and blood pressure increases; monitoring is required.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: on-label prescription TRT under federal Schedule III controls.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA approval and DEA Schedule III controls apply; state rules not separately verified.
access_records.legal_basis: FDA-approved testosterone products indicated for hypogonadism; testosterone is federally Schedule III (21 CFR 1308.13(f)). State-specific scheduling not verified.
access_records.regulatory_authority: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA); state medical and pharmacy boards

access_records.procedure_name: Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT) for Hypogonadism
access_records.access_pathway_details: Testosterone cypionate is an FDA-approved prescription drug. Próspera's rules allow use of products approved by a listed peer country such as the US, but only 'in the approved manner', so off-label use depends on the regime the practitioner elects. Honduras' Supreme Court declared the ZEDE laws unconstitutional in September 2024.
access_records.provider_requirements: Practitioners must make a regulatory election and secure informed patient consent that discloses their regulatory election and licensure status.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Próspera ZEDE: access relies on foreign (e.g., FDA) approval under the zone's contested regulatory-election system; no local availability was verified.
access_records.legal_basis: Próspera Health Industry rules let practitioners who elect Honduran or peer-country regulation use any pharmaceutical, device, procedure or biological agent approved by Honduras or a listed peer country (incl. the US), in the approved manner. Testosterone cypionate is an FDA-approved prescription drug.

access_records.procedure_name: Elamipretide / Mitochondrial-Targeted Peptides (SS-31 Class)
access_records.access_pathway_details: Federal FDA approval applies: Forzinity (elamipretide) is approved for Barth syndrome in patients weighing at least 30 kg and is dispensed through the exclusive US specialty pharmacy (AnovoRx). Other uses are investigational.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Approved indication: Barth syndrome, patients weighing at least 30 kg. Other conditions: trial or expanded-access criteria only.
access_records.provider_requirements: Prescription; supplied through the exclusive US specialty pharmacy (AnovoRx).

access_records.arbitrage_summary: Oregon: federal FDA approval applies (Barth syndrome, 30 kg and over); other uses are investigational.
access_records.oversight_notes: FDA accelerated approval; a post-approval randomized, placebo-controlled confirmatory trial is required.
access_records.legal_basis: NDA 215244 (Forzinity, elamipretide): FDA accelerated approval 19 Sep 2025 for Barth syndrome in patients weighing at least 30 kg; post-approval confirmatory trial required

access_records.procedure_name: Umbilical Cord Blood / Perinatal Cell Therapies
access_records.access_pathway_details: FDA-licensed cord blood (HPC, Cord Blood) is approved nationwide for unrelated-donor hematopoietic transplantation in disorders of the blood-forming system; cord blood, amniotic and Wharton's jelly products marketed for other conditions are unapproved.
access_records.eligibility_requirements: Patients with disorders affecting the hematopoietic system needing transplantation.
access_records.provider_requirements: Transplant programmes using FDA-licensed units or units under an IND.
access_records.risk_notes: FDA has received reports of blindness, tumor formation and infections from unapproved regenerative products.
access_records.arbitrage_summary: Approved for hematopoietic transplant under federal licensure; regenerative perinatal-cell uses are unapproved.
access_records.oversight_notes: Federal FDA licensure (BLA) or IND required for unrelated cord blood.
access_records.legal_basis: Licensed HPC, Cord Blood BLAs (e.g. HEMACORD, Ducord, ALLOCORD, CLEVECORD) under PHS Act s.351; unrelated cord blood otherwise requires an IND; other perinatal products (Wharton's jelly, amniotic) are unapproved
